references.text: Balak son of Zippor is identified as the king of Moab, confirming his position as the sender of the message to Balaam.
Balak sends a message to Balaam requesting him to curse Israel, which forms the background for Balaam's conversation with God.
Balak sends another message to Balaam, confirming that he was the sender of the original request.
Balaam confirms that Balak, king of Moab, brought him from Aram to curse Jacob.
Joshua reminds the Israelites that Balak son of Zippor rose up against Israel and sent for Balaam.
Jephthah refers to Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, in his speech to the Ammonites.
Micah reminds the people what Balak, king of Moab, planned and how Balaam answered.
